result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.eulerian_circuit()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Find an Eulerian circuit in the graph if one exists. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L19803-L19868){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.eulerian_circuit() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} An Eulerian circuit is a closed trail that visits every edge exactly once, starting and ending at the same node. Uses Hierholzer's algorithm. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Optional[list[int]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : List of node IDs forming the Eulerian circuit, or `None` if no circuit exists. The circuit starts and ends at the same node. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} - Uses Hierholzer's algorithm: O(E) time complexity - Only returns a circuit if one exists (use is_eulerian() to check first) - For semi-Eulerian graphs (path but no circuit), use a pathfinding approach - The returned circuit is one of potentially many valid circuits ## Examples {.doc-examples} On a cycle graph, the circuit visits every node and returns to the start, so its length is always one more than the number of edges: ::: {#96b32a1c .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_cycle_graph(5) circuit = graph.eulerian_circuit() # Returns 6 (5 edges, plus the return to the start) len(circuit) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 6 ``` ::: ::: A path graph has no Eulerian circuit (only endpoints have odd degree, so there's no way to return to the start), and the method reflects that by returning `None`: ::: {#eb7f3115 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_path_graph(5) circuit = graph.eulerian_circuit() # Returns None (path has no circuit) circuit ``` ::: The same holds for directed graphs, as long as every node's in-degree equals its out-degree: ::: {#6db4c05b .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph(directed=True) graph.add_cycle_graph(5) circuit = graph.eulerian_circuit() # Returns 6 (visits 5 edges, then returns to the start) len(circuit) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` 6 ``` ::: :::
